newsitem.title: IRAQ: U.N. says it fails to solve arms issues with Iraq.
newsitem.headline: U.N. says it fails to solve arms issues with Iraq.

text.p: Iraq and the United Nations were unable to solve outstanding disagreements over Baghdad's compliance with U.N. disarmament terms despite three days of talks, chief U.N. weapons inspector Rolf Ekeus said on Saturday.

"We did not solve any substantive issues. There I must say there is a slight disappointment...But what we did achieve was agreement on how to proceed for the nearest future," Ekeus told a news conference in Baghdad.
Ekeus arrived in Baghdad on Thursday to try again to resolve remaining disarmament issues holding up the lifting of the international oil embargo on Iraq, imposed for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
He said the U.N. Special Commission (UNSCOM), which he heads, still had serious problems in its assessment of Iraq's arsenal in the areas of biological and chemical warfare.

He said about seven important issues were still unresolved in the chemical area and his commission had provided Iraq with "concrete proposals" on what was still needed to be done in the biological warfare sphere.
Ekeus said it was still possible to alleviate his commission's concerns and Iraq had promised to do its best to achieve this in the near future.
